title: IPv6 Preference on Dual-Stack Baseline
evidence_summary: Observed conformance in tested trial(s): 40/40 (100.0%) trials established IPv6 connection on dual-stack baseline without fallback. Scoped to recorded trial(s); does not infer general client compliance.
reasoning: RFC 8305 Section 3 specifies that implementations SHOULD prefer IPv6 for the first connection attempt when both A and AAAA resource records are resolved.

title: Immediate Fallback on Active Connection Failure (TCP RST)
evidence_summary: Observed deviation in tested trial(s): Subsequent attempt started in 68.8ms after initial attempt (< 10ms minimum interval), deviating from RFC 8305 §5 mandatory floor ('a subsequent connection MUST NOT be started within 10 milliseconds of the previous attempt'). Classified as a mandatory-floor deviation. Scoped to recorded trial(s).
reasoning: RFC 8305 Section 5 distinguishes mandatory requirements from recommended parameters: subsequent connection attempts MUST NOT start within 10 milliseconds of the previous attempt (mandatory floor to prevent congestion collapse), while Connection Attempt Delay has a recommended minimum of 100 milliseconds and a recommended maximum of 2 seconds. When an attempt actively fails (such as TCP RST), Section 5 recommends starting immediately without waiting for the CAD timer to expire, provided the 10ms mandatory floor is respected. Results between 10ms and 100ms meet all mandatory MUST requirements while falling outside the recommended minimum CAD timer; they are classified as recommended-range deviations and are not labeled as MUST violations.

title: Connection Attempt Delay Timer on Unresponsive Path
evidence_summary: Observed conformance in tested trial(s): CAD median 342.155ms meets RFC 8305 §5 mandatory floor (>= 10ms) and falls within recommended range [100ms, 2000ms] (target: 250ms). Scoped to recorded trial(s); does not infer general client compliance.
reasoning: RFC 8305 Section 5 distinguishes mandatory inter-attempt spacing (MUST NOT be smaller than 10ms) from recommended CAD timer parameters (SHOULD NOT be smaller than 100ms, recommended default 250ms, maximum 2000ms) on unresponsive paths.

title: Fast Fallback on Primary Path Delay Exceeding CAD
evidence_summary: Observed deviation in tested trial(s): IPv4 failed to win reliably or CAD violated timing bounds (39/40 won, median CAD 305.1ms).
reasoning: When the primary address family RTT (600ms) significantly exceeds the CAD timer (~250-300ms), the second connection attempt over IPv4 (20ms RTT) finishes setup first and wins.

title: Resolution Delay on Asynchronous A/AAAA DNS Arrival
evidence_summary: Observed deviation in recorded Chrome trial (trial-20261028171417-b2d83f2f): Browser waited ~503.48ms for delayed AAAA response and connected over IPv6, rather than initiating IPv4 fallback after the RFC 8305 §4 recommended 50ms Resolution Delay. Conclusion is strictly scoped to this recorded Chrome trial and does not infer general browser non-conformance.
reasoning: RFC 8305 Section 3 recommends a 50ms Resolution Delay when A arrives before AAAA. If AAAA does not arrive within this window, the client SHOULD initiate IPv4. In the recorded single Chrome trial, the client waited for the late AAAA response (~515ms after query, ~496ms after A response) before connecting over IPv6. This observed deviation documents specific trial behavior under lab conditions and is not an inference of general browser implementation characteristics.

title: Statefulness and Adaptive Past-Failure Caching
evidence_summary: Indeterminate: Unsupported check. PS-028 protocol enforces isolated, ephemeral browser user-data directories (--user-data-dir) wiped unconditionally after every trial to eliminate cross-trial caching contamination. Cross-session persistence cannot be measured under isolated single-trial protocol.
reasoning: RFC 8305 Section 7 permits implementations to remember past failure history. Because trials are executed with clean profiles to guarantee measurement independence, cross-trial statefulness cannot be evaluated.

title: Transport Applicability (SCTP, QUIC, Multipath)
evidence_summary: Indeterminate: Unsupported check. The PS-028 isolated dual-stack laboratory specifically instruments HTTP/1.1 over TCP. Alternate transport protocols (QUIC, SCTP) are out of testbed scope.
reasoning: RFC 8305 Section 8 discusses Happy Eyeballs across various transport protocols. The current testbed evaluates standard TCP socket connections.
